item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Kyle Larson sits on the brink of a historic third NASCAR Cup Series title with a commanding 67-point lead. Per Yahoo Sports , the Hendrick Motorsports driver only needs to score nine points at the Homestead-Miami Speedway finale to officially secure the championship. This margin is so large that he does not even need to win the race or lead any laps to take the trophy home. The virtual world is preparing to mirror this real-world drama with the iRacing Homestead Championship Special Event. This week’s sim race covers 400 miles, or 267 laps, on the same track where real drivers will fight for the crown. According to iRacing, the event features dynamic weather and both fixed and open setup options to test driver skill. The Math Makes It Hard For Challengers Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin face a nearly impossible task to catch Larson before the checkered flag falls. Bell sits in second place but trails by 67 points, while Hamlin is 70 points behind the leader. Per Yahoo Sports, even if Bell scores the maximum 76 points available in the race, Larson would still win the title by reaching that nine-point threshold. This means Larson can finish 28th or better without earning a single stage point and still lock up the championship. The pressure is entirely on his rivals to hope for a mechanical failure or a crash for the No. 5 Chevrolet. Bell finished 10th at Martinsville and Hamlin came in sixth, but neither could close the gap enough to change the odds. William Byron won the Xfinity 500 at Martinsville to jump to ninth in the standings, but he is not in the championship hunt. A pit strategy error that put Larson a lap down early in the race did not stop him from recovering. His ability to get back on the lead lap and finish ninth while holding the points lead shows why he is the favorite to win. Real Life And Virtual Racing Collide The iRacing event is scheduled for November 8 at 3:00 pm ET to match the timing of the real-world finale. According to iRacing, this is the first time since 2019 that Homestead-Miami Speedway will crown the real-world champions for the Cup, Truck, and Xfinity Series. The virtual race uses the current NASCAR Cup Series cars to ensure an authentic experience for sim racers. Shawn Conklin has dominated the iRacing Open season with 25 wins in 49 starts. He holds a lead of nearly 1,700 points over second-place Jacob Reid in the virtual standings. The Fixed Series is much tighter, with Maximillion Bianco leading but Nick Olsen within 200 points of the title. To participate in the special event, drivers must hold a Class C+ or Class D with a 4.0 Safety Rating. The iRacing eSports Network will handle the broadcast call for the top split beginning Friday at 9 pm ET. Fans can watch the action live at iRacing.com/live to see who takes the virtual crown. item.title: Brittany Mahomes Trashes Referees Over ‘Weak’ Penalty in Crushing Chiefs Loss
item.description: Brittany Mahomes, Patrick Mahomes Credit: Grant Halverson/Getty; Matthew Stockman/Getty NEED TO KNOW Brittany Mahomes is sharing her opinion about how the Chiefs-Broncos game ended The wife of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes criticized a key call late in the game The Chiefs were called for a false start, negating what would have been a game-winning touchdown and sending them back five yards Brittany Mahomes is taking offense about an officiating call that resulted in a Kansas City Chiefs loss on Sunday, Nov. 1. “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD,” Mahomes, 31, wrote in a post to her Instagram Stories. “Oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us.” She continued, “That’s the weakest call I have ever seen. You can’t tell me otherwise.” The call in question involved her husband Patrick Mahomes , who was moments away from leading the team to a win over the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. But refs called a false start on Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore, just before Mahomes hit Rashee Rice with what would have been the game-winning touchdown pass with four seconds left on the clock. Credit: Brittany Mahomes/Instagram The score was wiped away and the team was backed up five yards — all of which culminated in a clunky play in which the quarterback was sacked by Malcolm Roach and time expired. The Chiefs blew an 11-point fourth quarter lead and lost, 28-24, giving the Broncos the top spot in the division. After the game, Chiefs coach Andy Reid backed up Brittany’s assessment. “I didn’t see it,” Reid told reporters about the call. “That’s one man’s opinion. I just didn’t see it. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a] false start.” The Chiefs now sport a 5-2 record after consecutive losses, having lost to Seattle the week before. Brittany, who has a longstanding practice of defending her husband’s team, called out commentators earlier this season in the Chiefs’ first matchup against the Broncos. Shortly after they had their way with Denver in the season opener on Monday, Sept. 14, 31-10, she seemingly had the last laugh. “Oopsies,” Brittany wrote on her Instagram Stories that featured a screenshot of four game predictions from ESPN analysts, all of whom picked the Broncos over the Chiefs. item.title: What was Kimi Antonelli’s best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli ’s record-breaking Formula 1 world championship triumph was highlighted by many superb performances. But which one was his best? Antonelli duly wrapped up his maiden F1 crown in Mexico with four rounds to spare – becoming the youngest-ever world champion in the process. Our writers have picked out the moments they believe turned the Italian from a contender into a world champion in waiting. Melbourne crash response offered first glimpse of new Kimi – Filip Cleeren Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes It may sound odd to pick one of Antonelli's few defeats against Russell, but his runner-up spot to the Briton at the season opener in Melbourne showed me the first tranche of evidence that the Antonelli who had rocked up Australia wasn't the same insecure rookie who had struggled through spells of 2025. The Albert Park weekend was actually one of Antonelli's more challenging weekends, suffering a heavy 25G crash in FP3 that looked set to derail his weekend. It may have done a year prior, but this time the young Italian stayed cool and collected. And as Mercedes was able to pull off a full rebuild just in time for qualifying, Antonelli was able to shake off the incident and take second on the grid behind Russell despite not being able to finetune the car's set-up. In the race Antonelli then suffered from a poor getaway with no battery power as he was swamped and dropped to sixth, but Mercedes' pace advantage was thus that he was able to make a controlled recovery to second. "If something like that had happened to me last year, the rest of the weekend would probably have been very compromised," Antonelli reflected in Austin. "When you have one year of experience, one full year in Formula 1, you come back the next year and you just feel better. Things happen a bit more easily, let's say, also because you're not forcing them to happen as much. "I kind of took a step back in that regard and just tried to focus on the important things and enjoy the process as much as possible. Definitely, mentally I've been in a much happier place this year compared to last season. And especially when you've been working with the same group of people for one year, going into year two is a big difference as well. You know how to move on together as a team, especially from difficult situations." Canadian GP - Antonelli's real statement drive – Ewan Gale Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes By the time F1 had rocked up to the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, Antonelli had already proven that he possesses some of the traits needed to be successful. Yet this was the first real ding-dong battle we had seen between the Italian and an adversary that meant something. Fighting for the lead with Russell throughout the first half of the race, we saw that Antonelli was not going to be a pushover for his more experienced team-mate in the race for the title.

item.title: Stat of the Day: Mercedes Needs Only a 3-Point Edge on Ferrari in Brazil to Clinch the Constructors’ Title
item.description: Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Mercedes leads Ferrari 630 points to 504 with four Formula 1 rounds left. That 126-point gap looks like a runaway, and it is. The number that matters this week is smaller: three . That is how many points more than Ferrari Mercedes must score in the São Paulo Grand Prix to lock up the constructors’ championship at Interlagos. The math behind the stat A team can score a maximum of 43 points in a grand prix: 25 for a win and 18 for second place. There are no sprint races left, because all six 2026 sprint weekends (Shanghai, Miami, Montréal, Silverstone, Zandvoort and Singapore) are done. The remaining rounds are São Paulo (November 6-8), Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Once Brazil is over, three races will remain, so Ferrari’s ceiling is 3 x 43 = 129 points. If Mercedes leaves Interlagos 129 or more points clear, Ferrari cannot pass it. From a 126-point lead, Mercedes only needs to outscore Ferrari by three. A tie on points would also go to Mercedes on wins, which it leads 12 to 2 this year. What it reveals competitively Three points is a small ask. Mercedes has averaged about 33.2 points per round against Ferrari’s 26.5, a margin of roughly 6.6 per race. The target for Brazil is less than half of its normal edge. For Ferrari to stop the clinch it would need to beat Mercedes by four or more in a single non-sprint race, which in practice means a near-perfect Sunday with Mercedes stumbling at the same time. The split inside the points explains why. Mercedes’ 630 is Kimi Antonelli’s 380 plus George Russell’s 250. Ferrari’s 504 is Lewis Hamilton’s 259 plus Charles Leclerc’s 245. Russell and the Ferrari pair are within a few points of one another; Antonelli is the whole gap . He has won nine of Mercedes’ 12 races, while Ferrari has taken just two wins between its drivers. We broke down his title run in our earlier look at his points lead and his one-stop win in Austin . Photo by Jonathan Borba on Pexels.com Why the clinch matters beyond the trophy The constructors’ standings are where the money is. Final positions set the share of Formula 1’s prize fund, which we explained in how the constructors’ championship determines prize money . Mercedes had already been in the frame to take both crowns, as covered in Mercedes Can Win Both F1 Titles in Mexico City . Antonelli’s drivers’ title is secured, so Brazil is now about whether the team side can be closed out with three races still to run. What to watch in Brazil Ferrari’s one-two ceiling: only a Hamilton-Leclerc double podium combined with a Mercedes weak day keeps the title alive past Interlagos. Russell’s Sunday: Antonelli will score, so Russell’s finish decides whether Mercedes gets there comfortably. The fallback dates: if Brazil does not do it, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi each cut Ferrari’s maximum by another 43. item.title: Dodgers Breakout Star Projected to Crack MLB Roster in 2027
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have to change something before next season begins following their disappointing finish to the 2026 season, and Sonja Chen of MLB.com believes an extended run of games for Josue De Paula could go a long way. In her “way-too-early” look at the Dodgers’ roster for 2027 , Chen listed De Paula as the Dodgers’ starting left fielder. Why Would the Dodgers make Josue De Paula Their Starting Left Fielder? De Paula only has 11 regular-season MLB games under his belt, but looked like a seasoned player during his brief tenure in the bigs last season. He hit a monster home run against the Miami Marlins during those 11 games, bringing home a total of seven runs while posting a 1.081 OPS with a .500 on-base percentage. His performances during the regular season earned him a spot on both the NLDS and NLCS roster. But his defense remains a big question mark.” De Paula played well beyond his years in 2026, and giving him a shot in the majors next season would be a borderline criminal offense by the Dodgers. What is the Case Against Josue De Paula Starting? While his offensive capabilities are impressive and he almost certainly deserves a spot on the roster, starting as the Dodgers’ left fielder may be too much too soon for the rookie. item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake beats South Glens Falls for its 4th straight Section 2 Class B field hockey title
item.description: Burnt Hills celebrates after defeating South Glens Falls to win the Section 2 Class B championship on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) GLENS FALLS - When Grace Kogut and Katie Lansley were eighth graders on the 2022 Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake field hockey team, their first varsity season ended in devastation. That 2022 season ended the Spartans' run of nine consecutive Section 2 Class B championships. In the years since, Kogut and Lansley have been key contributors for the program, as it's begun a brand new stretch of dominance. On Sunday afternoon, Burnt Hills defeated South Glens Falls 6-1 to secure its fourth straight Class B championship. "A little bit, but I'm very confident in our team," Kogut, now a senior, said on whether she ever gets flashbacks from the championship game loss in 2022, which came against South Glens Falls. "Today we were ok, but there's definitely some bad memories there. "At least for me, I feel like after that loss, we wanted to push to get better. It was heartbreaking and I know we never wanted to feel like that again." In addition to Burnt Hills' four straight Section 2 titles, the Spartans are two-time defending Class B state champions and are set to return to the state tournament looking to defend their crown. "We're really proud of the team to get it up to four. Even though we had so many before and we lost (in 2022), it's really good to see us build it back up," Lansley said. "I think it's the team culture, and we're a family. We carry that on to the field. Every year, the team is so close on and off the field, and I feel like that really carries us." Burnt Hills' Katie Lansley navigates through the South Glens Falls defense during the Section 2 Class B championship game on Sunday at Glens Falls High School. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) Key moment Riley Rodecker got Burnt Hills on the board midway through the first quarter, and the Spartans kept the momentum the rest of the way. The top-seeded Spartans, who received a bye into the title game, scored two goals in the first quarter and two in the second, to take a 4-0 lead into the half against the second-seeded Bulldogs. They added another goal in the third and fourth quarters for a 6-1 victory. "We always tell them, ‘Next game,'" said Burnt Hills coach Kelly Vrooman. "I know we have this game (under control), but we have to look ahead to the next game, to stick to the details and (uphold) the standard we have here." Star of the game A mix of Burnt Hills' senior leaders and youngsters made an impact on the scoreboard on Sunday. While Kogut had two goals and an assist and Lansley had two assists, freshman forward Carah DiCaprio had the standout performance with three goals and an assist. Maeve McCarty punched in the lone goal for South Glens Falls in the third quarter, as she navigated her way down the field for an unassisted score. item.title: Daily Motorsport Briefing, Nov. 2: Antonelli Is Champion, and Ferrari Has a Mess to Clear Up
item.description: Photo by Paul Keiffer on Unsplash Kimi Antonelli is Formula 1’s champion, and the clean headline is hiding a messier Sunday behind it. Here is what the official series sources confirm as of Monday, Nov. 2, with results and schedules checked against Formula 1, NASCAR and MotoGP. The storyline that matters: Antonelli is champion, and Ferrari owns the mess Antonelli only needed ninth place in Mexico City. He finished on the podium, third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, and at 20 became the youngest World Champion in F1 history and the first Italian since Alberto Ascari in 1953. He leads Verstappen by 119 points with four rounds left. The race itself was a lesson in how a red flag resets everything: Mercedes left him out hoping for a Safety Car that arrived one lap after he had already pitted, then a barrier repair turned it into a red flag and a standing restart from fourth. He passed Leclerc at Turn 1 and spent the rest of the afternoon shadowing the leaders. Our earlier look at how Mercedes could win both titles in Mexico City set up this scenario, and the earlier worry about his illness in Mexico City never materialised on track. Ferrari is the story that will outlast the trophy. Hamilton took his first pole for the Scuderia and led down to Turn 1 before Leclerc went around the outside. Both ran off at Turn 4, Leclerc rejoined first, and Hamilton slipped behind Verstappen. Leclerc was given a five-second penalty, served it at the same stop as Verstappen, and lost the lead to him there. Hamilton finished second, 0.7 seconds behind. Leclerc has said he deserved the penalty, and team principal Frédéric Vasseur said Ferrari will sort the matter out internally. Verstappen’s sixth Mexico City win was his third victory in the last four Grands Prix, and it moves him to second in the championship on 261 points, two clear of Hamilton on 259. George Russell’s sixth place drops him to fourth on 250. With the title settled, the fight for runner-up is the live one. Photo by Amir Abbaspoor on Unsplash Results worth knowing In NASCAR, William Byron led 362 of 500 laps, swept both stages and won the Cup Series race at Martinsville by 2.049 seconds over Chase Elliott, his first win of 2026. The title picture is lopsided: Kyle Larson was ninth and now leads Christopher Bell by 67 points and Denny Hamlin by 70, with only those three still mathematically alive. Larson needs a finish of 28th or better, or simply nine points gained, at Homestead. Our Martinsville clinching preview laid out why a win was the only way to clinch there. Hamlin’s no-stop strategy in stage one cost him track position he never got back. In MotoGP, Marc Márquez won the Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang, with Pedro Acosta and Alex Márquez completing the podium after Alex took pole. item.title: Jonathan Taylor’s ‘foaming at the mouth’ admission about Colts goes viral
item.description: Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images Jonathan Taylor expressed his concern that other teams would be excited to play the Indianapolis Colts as they suffered their fourth straight loss of the season. The team went into the game on Sunday surrounded by trade talks about their star running back, Jonathan Taylor. He finished the game with 8 carries and rushed for 23 yards. It was an elite offensive display from the Jacksonville Jaguars as they posted 28 points in the first half alone and denied the Colts any scoring chance. Having lost their two key players, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, through trades, the Colts did not seem to have enough firepower to compete with the Jaguars on offence and defence. Jonathan Taylor makes worrying admission about Indianapolis Colts The Colts are 2-6 and in the middle of the four game losing streak. While they have traded away two key players, the team is expected to keep RB Jonathan Taylor. However, the player has expressed a major concern about the team after their loss to the Jaguars. “It’s not going to get any easier, it’s actually going to get even harder and teams are going to look at us foaming at the mouth. So then it comes to a point where what are you going to do? Your backs are against the wall? What are you going to do? and you know you have to fight your way out of the corner. That’s what I’m thinking about for myself but also how to convey that to the rest of the guys in the locker room that this is not going to get nowhere easier and we got to accept that; that’s just the first step,” said Taylor in the locker room. The Colts have a few winnable games coming up, with the Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles and the Tennessee Titans still on their schedule. They did lose to the Titans in October, but they should have secured the win, as even with all the difficulties this season, the Colts are an overall better unit than the Titans. If they are somehow able to keep Taylor in Indianapolis, the Colts could still record wins in these games. However, this is not something everyone is optimistic about, as he is a star RB and putting him on the trade block could get them some great future assets. Even with a few wins, the Colts’ season looks unsalvageable. While Taylor has maintained his stance of wanting to stay, the team could make a decision and move him away to officially start their rebuild. item.description: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is putting together a season for the history books. And following Sunday’s 19-15 victory over the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings, his name is now sitting alongside two of the greatest running backs in franchise history. Barry Sanders and Billy Sims. Not bad company for a 24-year-old. Gibbs rushed for 153 yards and a touchdown against Minnesota, helping the Lions improve to 5-2. But his performance was about much more than another 100-yard rushing game. He also established one franchise record and joined Sanders in an exclusive club that had stood for more than three decades. Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jahmyr Gibbs Passes Billy Sims in Lions Record Books According to the Lions’ official statistical update , Gibbs now has 1,058 yards from scrimmage through Detroit’s first seven games , surpassing Sims’ previous franchise record of 991 yards set in 1980. That’s 67 more yards than Sims accumulated through the same point of his legendary rookie season. Even more impressive, Gibbs has recorded at least 75 scrimmage yards in every game this season. He joins Sanders, who accomplished the feat in 1993, as the only players in Lions history to reach that mark in each of a season’s first seven games. For a franchise that has featured some of the most electrifying running backs in NFL history, that’s a remarkable accomplishment. Gibbs Joins Barry Sanders in Another Exclusive Club As if passing Sims wasn’t enough, Gibbs also made history with his 30-yard touchdown run against Minnesota. The touchdown was his 10th of the season, making him and Sanders the only players in Detroit Lions history to score at least 10 touchdowns in four consecutive seasons . Sanders accomplished the feat from 1989 through 1992. Gibbs has now done it in each of his first four NFL seasons, beginning with his rookie campaign in 2023. As we previously reported when Gibbs discussed his comparisons to Sanders , the young running back has repeatedly expressed his admiration for the Hall of Famer. And earlier this season, Sanders personally congratulated Gibbs after another record-breaking touchdown . Now, Gibbs has another accomplishment that connects him directly to the greatest running back in franchise history. The Scary Part? And with 10 regular-season games remaining, he has plenty of opportunities to continue adding to those numbers. item.description: Boxxer announced today that undefeated super lightweight contender Adam Azim will face veteran Gabriel Gollaz Valenzuela in a December 4th IBF eliminator at Copper Box Arena. Azim (15-0, 12 KO) has fought just once this year, a three-round drubbing of Steve Claggett that was less impressive for the caliber of opponent than for the method of execution. That’s kind of been the theme so far for his career; his last six have ended inside the distance, including over faded vets like Ohara Davies and Sergey Lipinets, but the breakthrough win has yet to arrive. Adam Azim said: “This is the biggest fight of my career. I’ve put in the hard work to get to this position and now it’s time to show everyone what I can do. Valenzuela is a toundeugh, experienced fighter and I’m preparing for the very best version of him. I know what’s at stake and I’m ready to deliver. My dream has always been to become world champion. This is the final test standing between me and that opportunity, and I’m not going to let anything get in my way.” Whether Gollaz (32-5, 18 KO) fits the bill is up for interpretation, but the guy can still fight. His current 2-2 skid doesn’t tell the full story, as he went toe-to-toe with Subriel Matias for eight round before succumbing and arguably deserved the win against Lindolfo Delgado last year . We know he’ll go for it, at the very least. Gabriel Gollaz Valenzuela said: “This is a massive opportunity for me. Adam Azim is a talented young fighter with a big future, but he has never faced anyone like me before. I’ve shared the ring with some of the best fighters in the world and that experience will make the difference on fight night. I know what it takes to compete at this level and I’m ready to show everyone what I can do. I’m coming to London to win. Victory will be coming home to Mexico with me.” This still being an eliminator suggests that the IBF has designs on rescheduling Delgado vs Arthur Biyarslanov for the vacant belt, or at the very least finding Biyarslanov a new dance partner. item.title: Russell ‘Distraught’; Gets Fined Post-Race After Antonelli’s F1 Championship
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Things are not well at Mercedes, and it cost driver George Russell some money Sunday. Russel once again fought his car’s energy delivery system, limped to a disappointing sixth-place finish, and had to watch teammate Kimi Antonelli become the youngest F1 champion in history when Antonelli finished third. Russell congratulated his teammate before the podium ceremonies, but bailed on his post-race media duties and immediately left the track. For bouncing in disgust, Russell received a €5000 (roughly $5600) fine . Russell ‘Distraught’ After Antonelli Claims Title No reason had been given for Russell’s absence in the post-race media sessions, but Mercedes CEO and Team Principal Toto Wolff has provided clarity on the situation. “I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he’s distraught about the situation,” Wolff told reporters. “It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi. I have known George for such a long time. He is going through a hard time, but he was also responsible in getting the young man into this team.” Wolff, who brought Russell into the Mercedes junior program back in 2017 and has overseen his career through both Formula 2 and Formula 1, supported him in his absence post-race. “I’m very much with him at the moment,” he explained. “I’ve been in situations where it’s very, very difficult to cope. So him not doing the media work or leaving the track is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me.” It’s been a long and difficult Formula 1 season for Russell, who was still mathematically in the title hunt until Antonelli crossed the line in P3. Seeing his chances at the championship end with four more races to go, it is understandable that he would not want to face questions from the media yet. Wolff: Mexico Mirrors Russell’s Season Russell had entered Sunday’s race with a chance at a victory, starting P2 behind former teammate Lewis Hamilton. Unfortunately for him, he had an energy deployment issue at the start that saw him drop back from the leaders. He then made contact with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar going into Turn 6 on the opening lap and received a 10-second penalty. He finished the race in P6, dropping 10 points, and slipping down to fourth in the Drivers’ Standings. Wolff spoke on what happened to Russell during the race, commenting that it was similar to his season as a whole, where the potential for success has been there, but performance and reliability of the car have had a negative impact. “For a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment, and maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season,” Wolff said. “This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car, and we let him down on the first straight. item.title: Real Madrid reach historic La Liga penalty milestone after Racing Santander victory
item.description: Real Madrid reach historic La Liga penalty milestone after Racing Santander victory Real Madrid continued their fine form at El Sardinero, securing an impressive 3-0 victory over Racing Santander. Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande scored the goals for Jose Mourinho’s side on the day. The Frenchman’s goal saw him score against his 24th different opponent in La Liga , but it came under controversial circumstances. Mbappe was awarded a debatable penalty, and questions have been raised about whether he dived. According to Mundo Deportivo , the penalty awarded to Mbappe at El Sardinero was Real Madrid’s 601st in La Liga history. This extended Los Blancos ‘ lead as the club with the most spot-kicks awarded in the competition. Former referee Eduardo Iturralde Gonzalez argued that the contact was insufficient to justify a penalty. Real Madrid lead historic La Liga penalty rankings Barcelona are second on the list, with 520 penalties awarded, followed by Atletico Madrid with 498. Los Blancos have received 81 more penalties than the next closest team and 103 more than their city rivals. Kylian Mbappe was awarded a soft penalty against Racing Santander. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The trend also extends into the 21st century. During this period, Real Madrid lead the rankings with 235 penalties. That puts them ahead of Barcelona with 204 and Athletic Club with 171. Interestingly, Atletico Madrid do not make the top three here. Do the statistics tell the complete story? Such numbers tend to prompt opposition supporters to make the lazy argument about favouritism towards Real Madrid. The total number of penalties awarded to Los Blancos does not automatically establish favourable treatment from referees. Real Madrid have always tended to have more unpredictable, pacy forwards who thrive in transition. Real Madrid have a lot of pacy forwards who tend to be trickery for opposition defences. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) There is a much higher chance of winning a penalty when running towards goal than when keeping possession for long spells. While some penalties, like the one against Racing, may come under scrutiny, such calls go in favour of every team. The important thing is that even without that penalty, Los Blancos played sublime football against Verdiblancos . Mourinho is getting his team purring at the perfect time, and it remains to be seen how they fare against AEK Athens in midweek.

item.title: Neuer and Olise back in Bayern team training ahead of Atlético clash
item.description: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer takes part in the team's final training session at the Saebener Strasse training facility ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League soccer match against Atlético Madrid. (is associated with: «Neuer and Olise back in Bayern team training ahead of Atlético clash») Sven Hoppe/dpa Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and forward Michael Olise returned to Bayern Munich team training on Monday. Both players joined the final training session ahead of the Champions League clash against Atlético Madrid on Tuesday. Neuer missed Saturday's 2-2 draw with Dortmund due to pain in his foot, while Olise had to come off after taking a knock during the game. Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl said Olise's situation is being taken "day by day" and that doctors will "take another look at him tomorrow." "It's good that he's travelling with us, because he's an outstanding player who's always a great asset. However, we'll avoid the risk of it turning into a long-term injury. Manuel Neuer has been out for quite some time but has been training, so we'll see how it goes," he said ahead of the team's departure to Madrid. The already injury-hit German champions also saw Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry picking up injuries during the clash against Dortmund. Saibari had surgery after he tore the syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle, while Gnabry sustained a muscular injury in his left hamstring. Against Atlético, Bayern will once again be led by assistant coach Aaron Danks, who's overseeing the team during Vincent Kompany's absence. Kompany has so far missed three games due to illness and it's unclear when he will return. Bayern still top the league standings on goal difference after the draw with Dortmund, but against Atlético "we need to show resilience," Eberl said. "We must keep going if we want to win major titles, and that's what we want. We want to win in Madrid. We're always under pressure, but we're still heading there to try to achieve the best possible result."

item.description: Shaun Edwards is now committed to Argentina for the 2027 Rugby World Cup [Shutterstock] Decorated defence guru Shaun Edwards says his offer to work for England at next year's Rugby World Cup was turned down by head coach Steve Borthwick. Edwards, 60, left his post with France earlier this year and, after a short-term role with England's women's side, has signed up to work with Argentina until the end of the tournament. "I had a good chat with Steve over the phone," Edwards told Rugby Union Weekly. "I said to Steve he can make me assistant kit man and I'll be there, I'll be ready for work. "He was very, very honest with me and I thanked him for that. "He said he was happy with his staff and the way things have been going, and I respected him for that." Edwards is one of the most successful defence coaches in the game, having won three Six Nations Grand Slams during a 12-year spell with Wales and then helping restore France as a global powerhouse - with three Six Nations titles secured on that side of the Channel. He also won two Champions Cups and four English titles during his time with Wasps, initially as a defence coach before taking on the club's top job. Edwards, who was a hugely successful rugby league star with Wigan and Great Britain in his playing days, has long been linked with England's men's side. Approaches were made by the Rugby Football Union to bring him into their coaching pathway in 2006 and 2008, while chief executive Bill Sweeney had informal talks with Edwards in 2021 but opted against competing with France for his services. Borthwick's backroom set-up is already set for Australia 2027, with Richard Wigglesworth overseeing defence, supported by Byron McGuigan and Joe El-Abd. England have endured fluctuating form over the past two years, with a 12-Test winning streak ended by Scotland in February and followed by five successive defeats.
